svg.title: Capability poster — six AI uses sorted into building and borrowing
svg.desc: A two-zone classroom poster. The upper zone lists three capability-building uses; the lower zone lists three capability-borrowing uses. Each row pairs the use with its one-sentence mechanism.
svg.text: Six ways students use AI.
Three build capability. Three borrow it. Same tool. Different cognitive operation.
Building — the cognitive work stays with you
use
why it works
Ask the AI to challenge your reasoning.
Triggers prediction error; builds the model.
Ask the AI to generate edge-of-competence problems.
Creates productive struggle; drives consolidation.
Run the Feynman test conversation.
Forces retrieval; reveals what is missing.
AI does adjacent work. You do load-bearing work. Storage strength builds.
Borrowing — the AI does the work that was supposed to build you
use
why it fails
Ask the AI to write the first draft.
Bypasses generative struggle that builds schema.
Ask the AI to summarize the reading.
Bypasses deep processing that builds comprehension.
Ask the AI to solve the problem.
Eliminates the productive difficulty that is learning.
Figure 14.5 — the test isn’t what you ask; it’s where the thinking happens.
